name: Judson LaMoure

updates.occupation: Merchant (Neche, Pembina Co.); Indian sub-agent; legislator

events.title: Sub-agent to the Brule Sioux
events.description: Settled at Elk Point 1862 in the transport business with H. D. Booge & Co.; appointed sub-agent 1865.

events.title: Dakota territorial legislature and North Dakota State Senate
events.description: Territorial Assembly from 1872, Council 1876, Territorial House 1880, State Senate 1889 until retiring in 1913; LaMoure County and the towns of LaMoure, Jud and Judson named for him.

bioAdditions:
Judson LaMoure was born 27 Mar 1839 at Frelighsburg, Lower Canada, the youngest of five children of John Edward LaMoure (1795-1869) and Lois Louisa Perry (1805-1881); his eldest brother Edward Byron LaMoure was killed in an Indian raid at Elk Point, Dakota Territory, on 9 Aug 1865. He came to Davenport, Iowa, in 1859, tried the Pike's Peak gold rush in 1860, and from 1862 was at Elk Point. He moved to Pembina County in 1870, kept a store at Neche, and sat in the territorial and then state legislature until 1913. He married Minnie Ella Nelson on 3 Dec 1874 (six children, four surviving), and died at Stuart, Florida, on 16 Mar 1918 (S1).

The 1919 Lamoureux Record only says the author 'thinks' the North Dakota LaMoures descend from Jacques/James Lamoureux (b. 1731, of Rensselaerville and Westerlo, Albany Co.), and that some of James's grandchildren adopted the spelling LaMoure (S2). Judson's Quebec birth is a caution: the same publication notes separate French-Canadian Lamoureux families (from Boucherville, 1660s) in Quebec, including at Bedford, near Frelighsburg (S2). Frelighsburg was also settled by Loyalists and New Englanders, so either origin is possible.
funFacts: In 1873 he led a rescue party into a blizzard to find laundresses and children left behind by Custer's 7th Cavalry (per Wikipedia).

confidenceRecommendation.justification: The descent from James Lamoureux (b. 1731) rests only on the 1919 author's opinion; Judson's birth in Quebec, close to French-Canadian Lamoureux settlements, means a non-Huguenot origin cannot be ruled out. Even if the 1731 line holds, he is a distant cousin (James was a brother of John Meier's ancestor Jean, b. 1723).

openQuestionsNew: Parentage of John Edward LaMoure (1795-1869): is he a grandson of James Lamoureux (1731-1821) of Westerlo, or of a Quebec Lamoureux family?

sources.citation: A. J. Lamoureux, The Lamoureux Record no. 1 (1919)
sources.supports: tentative descent from James (b. 1731); LaMoure spelling; French-Canadian Lamoureux families in Quebec
